title: How to See When Your SQL Server Backup or Restore Will Finish
summary: A SQL Server query shows the estimated completion time for active backup or restore operations by converting the estimated_completion_time value to a readable clock time. This helps database administrators know when long-running operations will finish instead of guessing.
key_points: SQL Server's sys.dm_exec_requests system view contains estimated_completion_time in milliseconds for active backup and restore operations
The query converts milliseconds to seconds and adds them to the current time using DATEADD to show an actual finish time
The estimated_completion_time value recalculates continuously as the operation progresses, giving a fresh estimate each query execution
The percent_complete column shows progress percentage, while estimated_completion_time answers when the operation will finish
VIEW SERVER STATE permission is required to access the underlying system views

quotes.text: SQL Server already knows roughly when it expects to finish. You just have to ask for it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains that the solution builds on existing SQL Server functionality rather than requiring new tools

quotes.text: tells you the one thing people actually care about, which is when this will be done.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies that estimated completion time directly answers the practical question DBAs need answered
